messages.subject: Re: messages between client and server
parts:
Capturing the inputs are easy. You could add this code to server.R, inside your server function:

observe({
  inputs <- as.list(input)
  # One example of saving, probably you'd want something more sophisticated:
  write.csv(inputs, "userinputs.csv", append=TRUE)
})

This would call write.csv with all the inputs whenever any one of them changed.

Saving the plot is harder. By far the cleanest route would be to take the inputs and re-generate the plots when you need them--if you factor your code into functions in a separate .R file, then this should be straightforward.

2013/3/13 Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com>
Capturing the inputs are easy. You could add this code to server.R, inside your server function:

observe({
  inputs <- as.list(input)
  # One example of saving, probably you'd want something more sophisticated:
  write.csv(inputs, "userinputs.csv", append=TRUE)
})

This would call write.csv with all the inputs whenever any one of them changed.

Saving the plot is harder. By far the cleanest route would be to take the inputs and re-generate the plots when you need them--if you factor your code into functions in a separate .R file, then this should be straightforward.
